title: How do you ensure AI-generated game music doesn't violate copyright?
author: dnr424
selftext:
How do you ensure the generated music doesn't unintentionally resemble an existing copyrighted track?

Are there any reliable tools or services that can scan AI-generated music for potential copyright issues before releasing a game on Steam?

Curious how you guys are handling this.

comments.author: xWranglerWranglerx
comments.body: Can’t you literally just change one note and be fine ?

replies.author: dnr424
replies.body: They can still sue us. They have the money & power.

replies.author: xWranglerWranglerx
replies.body: Probably I was just asking. This might be a good question for Claude

replies.author: tipsystatistic
replies.body:
More likely you get a cease and desist. If you’re getting sued it’s be your game was a massive success and made a bunch of money.  Nobody’s suing an indie dev with no money.

If the goal of the lawsuit is to stop infringement, they can accomplish that with a letter.  If the goal is to recoup millions in damages, you need to have millions to recoup.

comments.author: shitty_advice_BDD
comments.body: I just let it fly,they usually send a cease and desist letter first, then you just comply by removing whichever song they said was infringing. Then nothing happens.

replies.author: shitty_advice_BDD
replies.body: No, first thing that happens is they tell you to stop using it, so you do. Then its done and everyone is happy.

replies.author: dnr424
replies.body: I'm trusting you on this! Hope it's not what your handle says 😑

replies.author: shitty_advice_BDD
replies.body: Run our conversation through ai and ask it. That should tell you more than I can in a short exchange. There is some possibility of getting delisted but the usual route is, its recognized, they tell you to stop, you do and apologize and explain how it happened and most reasonable companies will be fine with it. They're not going to go balls to the wall against one person if that person immediately concedes.

comments.author: StoneCypher
comments.body:
this is an unrealistic fear.  i can't name a single game in history that has been walked on for copyright infringement of the soundtrack, and the standards are so tight that doing it by accident seems borderline impossible.

to me, this seems like being concerned what happens when a container ship strikes your mountain home

comments.author: DiscountCthulhu01
comments.body: It's ai, if you're worried about stealing from people or infringing in copyright through derivative works, you really shouldn't be using it to begin with.
